name: Mắm Cù Lao Chàm
summary: Mắm is the fish sauce islanders like with the rice. The Hội An World Heritage centre’s 16 September 2025 study says many households have stopped keeping a jar through the storm season, and that only a few still make it to sell to visitors. It prints no method and no price.
origin: Cham Islands. A household sauce on Tân Hiệp, no longer a jar in every kitchen.
howToEat: On the side of the seafood rice, if a household is still selling it. The 16 September 2025 study does not describe the fish or the ferment.
The reserve management board’s 3 March 2026 note still has forest greens dipped in mắm cái with chili and garlic. The 2025 study lists mắm cái among foods people rarely use now. Both stay.
A current price is Check on arrival.
where: The hamlets. The 16 September 2025 study names no shop.
seoTitle: Mắm Cù Lao Chàm — island fish sauce
seoDescription: Fish sauce a few households on Tân Hiệp still make for visitors. The 2025 study says the storm-season jar is mostly gone. A price is Check on arrival.
